key_insight: Neutral ethylenediamine removes excess surface tin and reconstructs tin–lead perovskites, improving electron extraction and suppressing interfacial nonradiative recombination.
engineering_relevance: Controlling molecular protonation and surface stoichiometry offers a route to more efficient methylammonium-free tin–lead perovskite solar cells.
method: Compare neutral ethylenediamine and protonated ethylenediammonium iodide surface treatments.
Use atomistic simulations to examine vacancy-assisted iodide migration and deprotonation.
Connect surface reconstruction and n-type character to electron extraction into C60.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% power conversion efficiency and simulations showing that subsurface iodide vacancies lower the energetic cost of deprotonation.
watch_item: Long-term operational stability and scalable control of tin removal are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
